frequency_question: How often do federal oversight principals follow through on stripping recognition from an established national accrediting body within a two-year window of initiating a major review?
membership_rule: Members are instances where a federal department or oversight agency formally initiated a review process regarding the recognized status of a major national educational or professional accrediting entity. Excluded are routine renewals without contested administrative friction or lesser sanctions short of full removal of recognition.

cases.name: Department of Education review and termination of ACICS recognition (2016-2016 initial decision, finalized later)
Department of Education review of ABA law school accreditation standards (historical challenges where recognition was maintained rather than revoked)
Department of Education review of American Academy for Liberal Education (AALE) recognition

provenance_note: claims 15 cases from only 3 named (5.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 3 named; estimated roughly 15 comparable federal accreditation challenge proceedings in modern administrative history.
known_gaps: Excludes minor advisory committee recommendations that did not proceed to formal secretarial review stages.
skeleton: Total administrative challenges to major accrediting bodies resulting in ultimate revocation vs total major challenges initiated
multiplier: 3 hits out of 15 comparable formal administrative challenges yielding a base rate frequency of approximately 20 percent.
validity_reason: The baseline administrative procedures governing agency recognition remain stable across standard executive branch operational frameworks, persisting until major statutory reform alters the Department of Education's authority.
